FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Art activity flashcards.

Twenty-seven supplies, twenty-seven things to make with them. Each card names one art-room item — the crayon, the paintbrush, the scissors — and prints one activity under its name: draw a picture with shapes, paint a bright background, cut out simple shapes. Each card page carries the card, its activity and one way to set it up tonight; each item also gets a full lesson and a printable twin in the library. Little hands start with the crayon and the stickers; the studio shelf grows from there.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    One supply, one afternoon

    Pick a single card — say, the crayon — and let it run the whole craft time: draw a picture with shapes, trade crayons, draw the same picture with eyes closed. One supply keeps cleanup to one box.

  2. 02

    Mystery supply bag

    Hide three cards in a paper bag, pull one out, name the supply and hunt the house for the real thing. Finding the stapler instead of the tape becomes its own comedy.

  3. 03

    Activity relay

    Deal four cards face down around the table. Everyone moves one seat, turns the card over, and does its activity for five minutes — then the bell rings and the art migrates.

  4. 04

    Card-memory gallery

    After a week of making, lay the used cards out like a gallery and match each artwork to its card. The deck becomes a diary of everything the week made.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Chalk Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      Chalk is the crayon of the outdoors: fat, dusty and impossible to hold wrong. It only asks for a sidewalk, a driveway or a wall you are allowed to mark. This card’s activity: draw a picture with shapes — a circle sun, a square house, a triangle roof.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Chalk! Let’s draw with shapes — a big circle for the sun, a square for the house, a triangle on top for the roof. What other shapes can our picture hold?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw one giant shape on the ground — circle, square or triangle — and let the child fill it with more shapes until the whole thing is a shape mosaic. Rain will wash the gallery clean, which is half the fun.

      Quick parent note

      Sidewalk chalk is bigger than writing chalk because small hands grip best around something chunky — the same reason toddlers’ first crayons are short and wide.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Clay Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Clay is the supply that turns drawing into building: it pushes, rolls, squashes and stands up. Nothing on the art shelf rewards patience the way clay does, because the animal arrives one pinch at a time. This card’s activity: shape a tiny animal — the card’s rabbit takes one ball, two ears and a lot of gentle squeezes.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Clay! Roll it, roll it, roll it — now we have a little body. Pinch two ears, press a nose — what animal is growing in your hands?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Start with one ball and let the child decide what it becomes. Keep a damp cloth nearby so the clay stays soft, and give the finished animal a name — named animals get siblings, and siblings mean the next round is already booked.

      Quick parent note

      Clay is one of the oldest art supplies on Earth — people were shaping small animals from it over ten thousand years ago, long before anyone had paper.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Colored Pencils Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      Colored pencils are crayons that grew up: sharper, quieter and full of side-of-the-lead tricks. They reward a light touch with soft color and a heavy hand with bold lines. This card’s activity: shade a simple object — lay the pencil almost flat and sweep color across an apple, a leaf or a cloud.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Colored pencils! Hold the pencil low and lay it down flat — sweep, sweep, sweep like the wind. Look, the apple is turning red from one side to the other!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw one big outline — an apple, a ball, a leaf — and shade only one side of it, dark to light. The object suddenly looks round, and the child has just invented 3-D without being told.

      Quick parent note

      The card spells the name the British way — coloured — and both spellings are correct; in the US we write colored, and the pencils answer to either name.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Cotton Balls Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      A cotton ball is a paintbrush that forgot to be a brush: no handle, no bristles, just fluff that holds paint and lets it go in soft puffs. It is the friendliest printmaker on the shelf for two-year-old hands. This card’s activity: dab paint to make clouds — bounce the cotton ball across the paper and watch the sky build itself.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Cotton balls! Dip, dip, dab — bounce the soft cloud across the paper. Puff, puff — our sky is filling up with paint clouds!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Clip a clothespin around a cotton ball to give the cloud a handle, then dab a whole sky. Blue paint for day, purple for storm, and one flat smear for the rainbow that always follows.

      Quick parent note

      Cotton grows on a plant as the fluff around its seeds — so every cloud painting really is made of a plant, which makes the art a little bit botany.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Craft Sticks Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Craft sticks are building blocks in disguise: flat, light and glued at the corners they turn flat art into standing art. Every popsicle was a craft stick first, which means the best supply box partly comes from dessert. This card’s activity: build a tiny frame — four sticks, four corners, one small masterpiece inside.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Craft sticks! Two sticks here, two sticks there — a little square house for our picture. Where should the frame hang?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Glue four sticks into a square and let the child decorate the frame before the picture goes in — frames deserve art too. A strip of tape behind the corners holds everything while the glue dries overnight.

      Quick parent note

      A craft stick is just a tongue depressor with better marketing — hospitals and kindergartens buy them by the same box.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Crayon Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      The crayon is where art begins for most people: it never dries out, never runs out of ink and works on paper, boxes, sidewalks and (regrettably) walls. The card’s activity: draw a colourful picture — the card says it that way, and any picture made with a whole box of colors earns the extra u.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Crayon! Pick your colors — red, orange, yellow, green! Draw the sun, draw a flower, draw a big wobbly something. A picture with ten colors is a RAINBOW picture!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tape three crayons together and draw with a triple line at once — then split them apart and see which marks each color made alone. The child has just met the idea that tools change the drawing.

      Quick parent note

      A single crayon can draw a line more than a kilometer long before it runs out — artists have measured, because of course someone measured.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Drawing Pad Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      A drawing pad is the one supply that is also a place: every page is a fresh room waiting for something to live in it. Loose sheets get lost; a pad keeps the week’s drawings as one growing book. This card’s activity: draw your favourite thing — the card spells it the UK way, and whatever the favorite is, the pad gives it a page.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Drawing pad! Open the book to a new page — now draw your favorite thing in the whole world. A dog? A truck? Pancakes? Fill the page with it!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Turn a page into a gallery: child draws the favorite thing in the middle, then you draw yours beside it, then trade pages and add one detail to each other’s picture. Two artists, one book, zero wrong answers.

      Quick parent note

      The spiral on the side is called coil binding, and it lets the pad fold flat or flip over the back — a small invention that made sketching on laps possible.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Easel Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+The studio shelf

      The easel is the piece of furniture that makes a child feel like a real artist: paper clipped upright, paint pots below, both hands free. Standing art also dries without smudging, which the household fridge deeply appreciates. This card’s activity: set up your artwork — clip the paper, load the brush, take the stand.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Easel! Clip the paper on tight, choose your paint, and stand like a real painter. Lean back a little — look at your work! Artists always step back to see the whole picture.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Set the easel by a window and paint what the child actually sees outside — the same tree, painted four times a year, becomes a diary that draws itself. No easel? Prop a clipboard on a chair back and the studio travels.

      Quick parent note

      Easel comes from the Dutch word for donkey — ezel — because, like a donkey, it carries the load while the artist does the work.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Eraser Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+The studio shelf

      The eraser is the art supply that makes trying again free: every line can have a second draft, so nobody has to be perfect on the first one. For young artists it is less about mistakes and more about second ideas. This card’s activity: erase and redraw a shape — the same spot on the paper gets two chances.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Eraser! Rub, rub, rub — the shape is gone! Now draw it again, even better this time. See? Paper gives us second tries. That is the secret power of the eraser.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw a circle, erase half of it, and redraw the missing part as a moon, a cookie with a bite, a letter C. One shape, three ideas — the eraser is the doorway between them.

      Quick parent note

      Before rubber erasers, people erased pencil with bread — soft white breadcrumbs rolled the graphite away, and some artists still prefer them.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Feathers Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Feathers are texture you can hold: soft on one side, smooth on the other, and every one is already colored by a bird. Glued onto paper they turn flat craft into something that flutters when it is picked up. This card’s activity: glue a colourful texture — the card’s own words, and one feather is all it takes to change a picture.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Feathers! Feel how soft — now a dot of glue, press it down, one, two, three. Our picture has real feathers! A bird that never flies off the page!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw a big bird body, then glue real feathers along the wing line, one row at a time. Count them as they land — the bird that ends up with fourteen feathers is the fanciest bird in the house.

      Quick parent note

      A feather’s colors come from both pigment and tiny structure — some blues and greens are made by the way light bends through the feather, not by dye at all.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Glue Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Glue is the supply that makes everything else joinable: paper to paper, feathers to cardboard, the whole craft drawer onto one page. It teaches the two-step skill every maker needs — place it, then wait for it. This card’s activity: make a paper collage — torn or cut paper pieces, arranged and glued into one big picture.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Glue! A little dot, a little dot — not too much! Press the paper down and count to ten. One, two, three... ten! Stuck forever. What comes next on our collage?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tear old magazine pages into strips and build a collage of one big shape — a tree, a whale, a letter of the child’s name. Dots of glue, not rivers: the child learns the difference the first time a river wrinkles the paper.

      Quick parent note

      White glue gets its grip by turning from wet to solid as its water evaporates — it is not really drying, it is the glue changing its whole personality.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Ink Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      Ink is the only supply that can come from the artist directly: one fingerprint is a stamp the child was born with. The card’s picture proves it — a whole heart made of one fingerprint pressed again and again. This card’s activity: make a fingerprint picture — press, lift, look at the swirl.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Ink! One little press with one little finger — look! The tiniest lines inside your finger made a pattern nobody else has. Press again — same pattern, new print!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Press a row of fingerprints and add legs, wings or hats with a pen — a caterpillar of thumbs, a flock of pinky birds. Every print carries the child’s own swirls, which makes it the most personal stamp in the world.

      Quick parent note

      No two people have the same fingerprints — not even identical twins — which is why police use them and why every print on the page is signed by you.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Markers Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      Markers are the loud instruments of the drawing drawer: fat lines, deep color, zero pressure needed. Where a crayon whispers, a marker announces — which is why the boldest pictures in the house are always marker pictures. This card’s activity: make bold colourful lines — straight ones, wavy ones, zigzag ones, all with one confident sweep.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Markers! Cap off — CHEK! Now draw a bold line... all the way across! Loud lines, quiet lines, wiggly lines. What sound does a zigzag make?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play a line orchestra: one long steady line (a hum), three short sharp lines (a drumbeat), a slow wavy line (a song). The paper becomes sheet music, and the marker plays it.

      Quick parent note

      Markers feed ink from a soft tube inside by capillary action — the same way a paper towel drinks up spills — so the tip never needs squeezing.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Paintbrush Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      The paintbrush is the upgrade that turns coloring into painting: long sweeps, big washes and color that covers the whole page instead of sitting in lines. This card’s activity: paint a bright background — fill the whole paper first, before anything is drawn on it, so the picture starts on a sky’s worth of color.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Paintbrush! Dip in the paint — swoosh across the paper, all the way to the edges! We are painting the SKY first. The background comes first, and then the picture lands on top.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Paint the whole page one bright color and let it dry, then draw on top with crayon — crayon on paint is a picture with a sunset inside it. Big brush for backgrounds, small brush for details: that is the studio rule.

      Quick parent note

      Brushes have been made from hair for thousands of years — squirrel, goat and pony hair are still the classic soft brushes, and a good brush can outlive its artist.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Palette Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      The palette is where colors stop being separate and start making new ones: every spot is a tiny laboratory. Two paints and a thumb hole turn a painting session into color chemistry. This card’s activity: mix two colours together — the card’s own challenge, and the answers are endless.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Palette! Here is red, here is yellow — swirl them round and round... ORANGE! You made a brand-new color! What happens if red meets blue instead?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Mix one drop of white into each color on the palette and line the originals next to their paler twins — a wall of light versions. Then try the dark side with one drop of black, and let the child name the inventions.

      Quick parent note

      Painters once mixed colors on anything flat — tiles, shells, plates — until someone added the thumb hole; the missing slot in the palette’s edge is where the thumb goes while the hand holds on.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Paper Plate Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      A paper plate is a face before it is a plate: already round, already smiling-shaped, waiting for eyes. It is the sturdiest canvas in the craft box and the only one shaped like a head. This card’s activity: turn it into a funny face — eyes, nose, mouth, and whatever else a funny face needs.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Paper plate! Turn it over — look, it is already a face shape! Where do the eyes go? High up! Where is the nose? In the middle! Now the silliest smile ever!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Build the face in layers: draw it, then glue on button eyes, yarn hair and a paper-tube nose. Hold it up to your own face and let the plate talk — funny voices are what turn craft time into theater.

      Quick parent note

      The paper plate was invented by accident in the early 1900s when a worker at a Valentine card company noticed scraps of card were perfect for carrying lunch.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Paper Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      Paper is the supply that started it all, and folding is the way it becomes sculpture: no glue, no scissors, just hands and creases. The card’s orange dog started as one flat square. This card’s activity: fold a simple animal — two folds make ears, two more make a tail.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Paper! Fold it this way... and this way... open the ears — look, a puppy! What should our paper animal be called? Every fold changed the paper into something new!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Fold a square in half corner to corner for a triangle — that triangle is a cat with two fold-up ears, and it stands on its own. Add whiskers with a pencil and the whole animal took one minute.

      Quick parent note

      Folding paper into animals is called origami — Japanese for folded paper — and the strictest origami rule is one square sheet, no cutting and no glue at all.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Pencil Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      The pencil is the quietest and most honest drawing tool: gray lines, easy corrections, no color to hide behind. Faces are its favorite subject because three circles and a smile are enough to make somebody you know. This card’s activity: sketch a simple face — an oval, two dots, one curved line.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Pencil! Draw a big oval — an egg shape! Two eyes, a little nose, and a mouth. Is it smiling? Is it surprised? You just drew a PERSON!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw the same face three times with three mouths — happy, surprised, grumpy — and watch one sketch become three feelings. Add a mirror: the child draws their own face, which is the hardest and funniest portrait of all.

      Quick parent note

      A pencil’s gray center is graphite mixed with clay, and the little number on the side — HB, 2B — tells you the recipe: more clay makes a harder, lighter line.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Ribbon Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Ribbon is a line you can bend: shiny, floppy and made for curves that pencil lines can only imitate. On paper it becomes a collage of real curvy lines the finger can follow. This card’s activity: make a colourful line collage — ribbons bent, looped and glued into roads, rivers and rainbows.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Ribbon! Look how it bends — swoop! Make a big loop, now a squiggle, now a zigzag. A dot of glue... and the ribbon stays exactly where we put it. Our picture has REAL lines!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Glue ribbon lines onto paper and turn them into a picture: one ribbon becomes a road for a drawn car, another becomes the tail of a drawn kite. Then hold the leftover ribbon high and run — because ribbon play is air play.

      Quick parent note

      Ribbon loops stay flat because of a woven edge called the selvedge — without it, ribbon curls and twists, which is exactly the trick gift boxes use.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Ruler Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+The studio shelf

      The ruler is the supply that proves hands and edges are a team: held tight, it turns a wobbly line into a perfectly straight one. It is also the art shelf’s quiet math teacher — every line comes with numbers on it. This card’s activity: draw three straight lines — hold the ruler firm and let the pencil ride the edge.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Ruler! Press it down flat — one hand holds, one hand draws. Whoosh — a perfectly straight line! Two more... three! Nobody’s line is straighter than ours today.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw three straight lines and let the child tell you what they become: a table needs four, a road needs two, a ladder needs a dozen. Then flip the ruler over and connect the tick marks — the numbers are already a counting game.

      Quick parent note

      Rulers were among the first tools humans ever made — carved bone and ivory rulers over two thousand years old have been dug up, and they already had tick marks.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Scissors Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Scissors are the first real tool most children learn to drive: two handles, one thumb up, and the paper parts company with itself. Cutting is also quiet strength training for the hand that will one day hold a pencil. This card’s activity: cut out simple shapes — circles, squares, triangles, snipped one careful snip at a time.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Scissors! Thumb on top — open... close... snip! Look, a circle is being born! Slow snips make the shape smooth. What shape comes next?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw a fat triangle, a square and a wavy snake line, then cut all three. The snake is the graduation exam: wavy lines are where scissor hands become steady. Snippets do not get wasted — they become the confetti pile for tomorrow’s glue.

      Quick parent note

      Scissors are two wedges (blades) working as one machine — every snip is a lever and an edge at the same time, which is why cutting paper feels so much easier than tearing it.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Sponge Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      The sponge is the stamp that fits a whole fist: dip it, press it, lift a perfect square of color. One sponge plus one color can wallpaper a page faster than any brush. This card’s activity: print a repeating pattern — press, lift, press again, and watch the same shape march across the paper.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Sponge! Dip in the paint — press down... lift! Look, a print! Again — press, lift, press, lift! Same shape again and again: that is called a PATTERN.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Cut a dry sponge into small shapes with cookie-cutter edges — a square, a heart, a star — and print rows of each. Every press lands slightly crooked, and the crookedness is what makes sponge prints look handmade, because they are.

      Quick parent note

      Sponges are sea animals — real ones grow on the ocean floor — and the art sponge’s holes are exactly what held water when the animal was alive.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Stamps Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      Stamps are pictures that repeat themselves: one press equals one finished shape, perfect every time. The card’s stamp prints stars, and the row of five proves the best part — the same image, marching in line. This card’s activity: print a row of shapes — ink the stamp, press down hard, lift straight up.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Stamps! Press in the ink — tap, tap. Now press on the paper — push down hard and... LIFT! A perfect star! Again! A whole ROW of stars, all the same!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Print a border around a page’s edge — one shape, one row per side — and the next letter written inside it becomes a decorated letter. Then mix two stamps and let the child invent the repeating rule: star, flower, star, flower.

      Quick parent note

      Stamps changed the world before they ever reached a craft box — the first postage stamp, the Penny Black in 1840, was a sticker that let a letter travel anywhere for one penny.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Stencil Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Draw & color

      The stencil is the helper that guarantees a shape: hold it down, trace the hole, and out comes the star, the heart or the letter you were after. It is how young artists draw things their hands cannot freehand yet — and the pride is just as real. This card’s activity: trace a simple shape — the card’s star is waiting inside the outline.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Stencil! Hold it down tight with one hand — the shape is hiding inside. Trace around the edge... lift it up — a perfect star! Your hand did that!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Trace the same stencil twice, sliding it a little the second time, and color the space between the two outlines — the shape grows a rainbow echo. Letters work the same way: stencil the child’s initial, then fill it with marker dots.

      Quick parent note

      Stencils are at least 30,000 years old — cave artists blew paint around their own hands, which is exactly a stencil, made with a hand instead of plastic.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Stickers Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Stickers are art with the hard part removed: the shape is already perfect, the glue is already on, and success is one peel away. For the smallest artists they are the first supply that works every single time. This card’s activity: make a simple picture — peel a sticker, place it down, and build a scene one sticker at a time.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Stickers! Peel it — see the shiny back? Press it on the paper... stuck! Another one, and another — look, our stickers are making a picture! What is it becoming?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Draw a big scene lightly in pencil — a garden, a road, the night sky — and let the stickers move in as the stars, the cars, the flowers. Peeling the backing is the finger gym; placing them without overlap is the puzzle.

      Quick parent note

      The sticky part of a sticker usually has no glue at all — it is made of millions of tiny suction-like beads that grip by pressure, which is why stickers stick best when pressed firmly.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Tape Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Cut, stick & make

      Tape is the fastener that asks no patience: rip, press, done. Where glue needs drying time, tape needs one thumb, which makes it the youngest builder’s favorite tool in the box. This card’s activity: join two paper shapes — two squares, one strip of tape, and the shapes become one construction.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Tape! Rip off a piece — rrrrip! Press it across both papers — pat, pat, pat. Look! Two papers are holding hands now! What can tape join next?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tape paper strips into links and build a paper chain — every link is one rip, and the chain grows longer than the child, which is the goal every time. Colored tape on plain paper also makes roads, rails and racing tracks for toy cars.

      Quick parent note

      Tape was invented for car painters in 1925 — masked-off lines meant two-color cars — and it went from garages to kitchen drawers in about a year.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Art Activity Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · ART ROOM · AGES 2–5 YEARS

      Watercolors Flashcard for Toddlers

      Ages 2+Paint & print

      Watercolors are paint with the volume turned down: dipped in water, they glide in soft washes that overlap and blend like weather. They teach the big painting secret early — more water means softer color. This card’s activity: paint a soft sky — watery blue, one wide sweep at a time, until the page is weather.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Watercolors! Brush in the water first, then the paint — sweep it across, soft and slow. A little more water... even softer! Our sky is turning into a real one.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Paint the sky wet-on-wet: brush clean water over the paper first, then touch color into the wet and watch it bloom by itself. Drop one extra dot in the middle and call it the sun coming out — the water does the painting.

      Quick parent note

      Watercolors come in pans (little dry cakes) and tubes; the pans in the card’s box wake up with one drop of water and have been used by painters for over a century.

      Teach it, step by step
